The most powerful refutation is the “swine objection” (Mill’s reply to Bentham): if pleasures differ only in quantity, then a satisfied pig’s life could rank above a dissatisfied Socrates’s, which clashes with our considered judgments about higher and lower pleasures. This exposes the calculus’s failure to capture qualitative distinctions and its implausible reduction of all value to a single hedonic scale.
